column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2), 1.8.0: one Application content (version 0) that carries the 1.8.0 code and data, no separate update. In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive, Havok 2023.2), SDK 21.4.0 built for the Switch 2 (spec Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK movie 21.4.0)
# + subsdk1 (nn::ecli, Nintendo's embedded Mono runtime; main imports its allocator) + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code), as Donkey Kong Bananza.
# The 1.8.0 dump is version 0 as the earlier base-game dump was, so it takes the v0 row: the earlier build (main 9e244438c3d8ef1c703a6a85ef99c4f0, subsdk0 d39a7a3d44530bb6..., the ecli module
# that 1.8.0 loads as subsdk1, sdk 90ebba182862b9ec..., SDK 19.3.3) had no build-keyed cuts or host fixes and is not registered any more (README, Builds)
# Line 4 of System/RegionLangMask.txt is the build ID of the main its RomFS was made for (1.8.0: line 3 "180", line 4 d00e4f39...), as in Donkey Kong Bananza: a dump whose
# RomFS is another build's data under 1.8.0's code (GitHub #27 / #44: CRASH sig=11 at main+0x8bfc0 1.7 s in) is refused at Add / Prepare and on the card
# The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource (virtual address memory on; 1.8.0's NPDM differs only by the services chat:u, mnpp:app and stpl:u). nninitStartup sets the heap to the
# free application memory less a fixed reserve (main+0x84790: 0x5dc00000 in 1.8.0, 0x60400000 in the earlier base build, whose Mac heap check measured 0x1dbc00000): 0x1de400000
# (7.47 GB) in 1.8.0, by that formula (not measured), within the 7.75 GB heap region.
# The alias region holds the SDK's AddressRegionManager node area (0x3fe00000) and then the regions the game maps physical memory into (earlier base build: main+0x68524c), past +1.6 GB within 8 s
# of boot (DM_REGIONS, Switch-sized DM_ALIAS_SIZE); with a 1 GB alias region the first ones got no address and the game read a null object (main+0xc10170). 4 GB: the node area
# and the 1.57 GB (1.53 GB in 1.8.0) the 9 GB pool leaves beside the heap, with room for fragmentation. The Switch 2's 9 GB pool (as Donkey Kong Bananza; not measured)
# The reserve beside the heap goes to the game's virtual address heap, whose free size is what the system reports free (main+0x5a8c60 in 1.8.0: nn::os::QueryMemoryInfo
# total - used, page-aligned, less a page; GetInfo 21 / 22). On Horizon the used memory counts the pages mapped in the alias region; without this key the host leaves them out, so
# the heap's free size never falls and its blocks are never let go (kartnative on 1.0.0: 954 regions of 0xb1000 bytes by a fourth race, each a 512x512 R16 texture of 10 levels
# with its GPU copy; 2.4 GB mapped vs 1.25 GB with the limit; plumber-racer-2 sets it too). With it the used memory counts them and a map past the pool fails, as on Horizon:
# the heap (pool - used - 0x5dc00000) leaves the alias region the 1.5 GB reserve
# The framework (procFrame, main+0x69cbb0 in 1.8.0) runs a whole number of fixed 1/60 s steps each frame (the count at +0x214, which every update loops) and presents at that many
# vsyncs; its mode at +0x210 picks the count (0 = 1, or 2 when its own work overran; 1 = 1; 2 = 2, its 30 fps form for three or four players; other values keep the count).
# The frame rate cap writes the mode (60: the game's own, 30: 2, 20: 3 with the count 3), so the race keeps full speed at 30 and 20 fps (hle_fpslock.c steps_tick; README, Frame rate cap).
# The framework is at [[main+0x37c8410]+8] (the race's step loop at main+0x23fd36c reads it there)
# Large block-compressed textures from the game's files kept without their finest level on the Vulkan replay (Android; README, Memory): ported from plumber-racer-2 (MIT,
# copyright seedds), where it made a race fit an iPhone 18 Pro. Textures the game copies from stay whole (its terrain arrays are filled by copies: the road went purple without it)
# agl's render buffer binding: Donkey Kong Bananza's clears are wrapped in render conditions; the same engine, not yet checked on this game
# The 3D scenes' size follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale, not the window (README, Render resolution): the Android launcher's Game resolution
# sets these instead of DM_WINDOW_SIZE. <choice> <DM_GRAPHICS_SCALE> <operation mode>: handheld scale 0 crops 1920x1080, handheld scale 2 1280x720 (phone rH0 / rH2);
# Original has no row: the game's own (console, scale 1: 2048x1152). Phone 1440p is that same console scale 1 (2048x1152, the largest size the game draws). A choice with no row
# takes the largest row that fits in it, or the smallest (Phone 540p / 480p: 1280x720; Profile.resolutionEnv)
